## 1. Scope & site-specific context

**What is being done.** A mobile alloy access tower is erected against the south elevation to give safe working access to levels 2–4. Existing cladding panels are removed and replaced; a MEWP supplements the tower for outreach/elevation positions the tower footprint cannot safely reach. Materials are raised and lowered by gin wheel/hoist. On completion the tower is dismantled and the site cleared.

**What makes this site high-consequence.**
- A **live public footpath** runs directly beneath and alongside the work face — uninvolved members of the public are exposed to **falling objects and plant/pedestrian conflict** they have not consented to. This is the single dominant risk driver and shapes every control below.
- The building is **occupied** — occupants and other trades on adjacent elevations are exposed; work is **simultaneous (SIMOPS)** and must be coordinated, not assumed clear.
- Cladding on an existing building of unknown age/spec carries a **latent asbestos-containing-material (ACM) risk** in panels, fixings, sealants or backing — a **pre-start hold point**, not an in-work control.

**Pre-start hold points (do-not-start until all cleared):**
1. **[GAP — HOLD]** A **refurbishment/demolition asbestos survey** covering the south-elevation cladding, fixings, sealants and backing is confirmed present and clear. If ACMs are identified, **stop** — this RAMS does not cover asbestos removal; licensed removal under CAR 2012 is required first. *Owner: Site Manager — confirm before 8 July 2026.*
2. A valid **highway authority licence / temporary footpath closure or diversion** (Highways Act 1980) for occupying the public footpath is in place. *Owner: Site Manager — confirm before 8 July 2026.*
3. A **ground-bearing / firm-and-level base assessment** for the tower base and MEWP set-up positions (including any voids, basement, or service covers below the footpath/hardstanding) is signed off by the **Temporary Works Coordinator**. *Owner: Temporary Works Coordinator — confirm before 8 July 2026.*

## 2. Risk matrix key (org 5×5, multiply)

**Likelihood (L):** 1 Rare · 2 Unlikely · 3 Possible · 4 Likely · 5 Almost certain
**Severity (S):** 1 Negligible (first-aid) · 2 Minor (medical treatment) · 3 Moderate (lost-time / RIDDOR) · 4 Major (specified/serious injury) · 5 Catastrophic (fatality/multiple)

**Score = L × S. Bands:** **1–4 Low** (acceptable — monitor) · **5–9 Medium** (tolerable — reduce so far as reasonably practicable) · **10–15 High** (robust controls + hold point required) · **16–25 Critical** (do not proceed until reduced).

Controls are ranked by the **hierarchy of controls** — **Elim**ination → **Sub**stitution → **Eng**ineering → **Admin**istrative → **PPE**. No control set relies on PPE/administration alone without a higher-order control or a recorded justification.

## 4. Method Statement — sequenced safe system of work (8 steps)

The safe system of work below is executed **in order**. Each step lists its plant, the competency card that gates it, the permit(s) required, the step-specific controls, and the RA rows those controls satisfy. **The exclusion zone / footpath protection established at Step 1 is maintained continuously until Step 8** and is never stood down mid-works.

### Step 1 — Mobilise & establish the footpath exclusion zone
- **Plant/equipment:** delivery vehicle, pedestrian barriers, signage, covered walkway components, hand tools.
- **Competency:** Site Supervisor (**SMSTS/SSSTS**); banksman.
- **Permit(s):** highway authority footpath **licence/closure** (Highways Act 1980) confirmed present *(hold point)*.
- **Controls:** Confirm the three pre-start hold points are cleared. Close/divert the footpath if licensed; otherwise erect the **barriered, signed pedestrian exclusion zone / covered walkway** segregating the public from the full work face and the load-out/drop zone. Banksman controls all vehicle and plant movement; deliveries off-peak; mechanical offload; designated lay-down. Brief the crew (§8) and record signatures before any work at height begins.
- **RA-refs:** RA-01, RA-02, RA-03, RA-16.

### Step 2 — Inspect and erect the mobile alloy tower
- **Plant/equipment:** mobile alloy tower components, sole boards, stabilisers, tower tag.
- **Competency:** **PASMA-trained** operative (Tower Erector); Temporary Works Coordinator for base sign-off.
- **Permit(s):** **Working at Height / suspended-access permit** issued and live.
- **Controls:** Set the tower on the TWC-signed firm/level base with sole boards; deploy stabilisers/outriggers; tie/ballast per supplier where the height:base ratio requires. Erect by **AGR or 3T** so the operative is never on an unguarded platform; fit guardrails and toeboards at every lift. On completion, the competent person **inspects and tags** the tower (green) — it is **not used until tagged**. Maintain the Step 1 exclusion zone below; brick guards/toeboards fitted.
- **RA-refs:** RA-04, RA-05, RA-06, RA-07, RA-17.

### Step 3 — Transfer materials to the work level
- **Plant/equipment:** **gin wheel / hoist** (LOLER-examined, SWL marked), tag lines.
- **Competency:** **Appointed Person** for the lifting operation; PASMA operative on platform.
- **Permit(s):** Working at Height permit remains live; lift within the permit conditions.
- **Controls:** Raise materials by the **rated hoist** — no manual carry up the tower. Loads within SWL and platform SWL; distribute the deck load; take up only what the immediate task needs (no bulk staging). Exclusion zone directly beneath the drop line; loads secured and tag-lined; no person under a suspended load.
- **RA-refs:** RA-02, RA-07, RA-08, RA-09.

### Step 4 — Remove the old cladding panels
- **Plant/equipment:** hand/power tools (110 V/battery, PAT-tested), hoist for lowering, tool tethers, debris netting.
- **Competency:** Site Supervisor; PASMA operative(s); RPE-face-fit record if any residual dust risk.
- **Permit(s):** Working at Height permit; **asbestos survey clearance confirmed** *(hold point — do not disturb any panel until confirmed clear)*.
- **Controls:** **Confirm RA-11 asbestos hold point clear before touching a panel.** Work within the guarded platform — no leaning beyond guardrails; use the MEWP (Step 5) for positions the tower cannot reach. **Controlled lowering** of removed panels by hoist — nothing dropped; sequence removal so no free edge is left over the public; tool tethers; deburr/cap protruding fixings. Maintain exclusion zone and debris protection.
- **RA-refs:** RA-07, RA-09, RA-10, RA-11, RA-12, RA-16, RA-19.

### Step 5 — Position the MEWP and fit the new panels
- **Plant/equipment:** MEWP (boom/scissor, LOLER-examined), spreader pads, harness + restraint lanyard, new panels, hand tools.
- **Competency:** **IPAF-certified** operator (correct category — 1b boom / 3a scissor as applicable); trained ground rescue person; banksman.
- **Permit(s):** Working at Height / suspended-access permit covering MEWP operation.
- **Controls:** Set up on the TWC-assessed firm/level ground with spreader pads and outriggers deployed; away from footpath edges/service covers. Operator wears a **full-body harness on a short restraint lanyard** to the basket anchor (work restraint — prevents reaching a fall/eject position). Plan basket positioning to avoid **overhead trap zones** (RA-14); ground rescue person on standby at the auxiliary controls (§7); banksman during tracking; survey clear of overhead services. Coordinate with occupants/other trades (SIMOPS) — no over-under working.
- **RA-refs:** RA-07, RA-10, RA-12, RA-13, RA-14, RA-15, RA-16, RA-17.

### Step 6 — Inspect the completed work
- **Plant/equipment:** tower platform or MEWP for access.
- **Competency:** Site Supervisor; PASMA/IPAF operative for access as used.
- **Permit(s):** Working at Height permit remains live until access equipment is struck.
- **Controls:** Inspect from within the guarded platform/basket — no leaning out. Confirm all new panels and fixings secure before any access equipment is removed. Record inspection.
- **RA-refs:** RA-10, RA-17.

### Step 7 — Dismantle the tower
- **Plant/equipment:** tower components, hoist, tag lines.
- **Competency:** **PASMA-trained** operative (Tower Erector).
- **Permit(s):** Working at Height permit live until dismantle complete.
- **Controls:** Dismantle by the **reverse AGR/3T sequence** — never strip a guardrail before the operative has descended to the level below. Lower components by hoist or hand-to-hand — **nothing dropped**. Maintain the exclusion zone below until the tower is fully down. Team lifts for load-out.
- **RA-refs:** RA-02, RA-04, RA-07, RA-10, RA-17.

### Step 8 — Clear the site & stand down the exclusion zone
- **Plant/equipment:** delivery/waste vehicle, barriers, covered skip.
- **Competency:** Site Supervisor; banksman.
- **Permit(s):** close out Working at Height permit; retain footpath licence until reinstatement complete.
- **Controls:** Load out and segregate waste to **licensed disposal with transfer/consignment notes** (hazardous stream separate). **Staged, controlled stand-down** of the exclusion zone — final housekeeping and footpath surface **inspection before the public are readmitted**; banksman controls final plant movements. Permit closed and RAMS reviewed for lessons.
- **RA-refs:** RA-01, RA-02, RA-03, RA-19.

## 6. Public protection & exclusion-zone controls (dominant risk)

Because uninvolved public are exposed beneath the work face, these controls are treated as **primary, not supplementary**, and are audited daily by the Site Supervisor:

- **Segregation first (elimination):** footpath **closure/diversion** under the highway licence is the preferred control. Where the authority will not permit closure, a **fully barriered pedestrian exclusion zone with a covered walkway/fan** separates the public from the work and drop zones — the public are never routed under an unprotected work face.
- **Falling-object defence (engineering):** toeboards, brick guards, debris netting, and a protective fan/covered walkway; controlled hoist lowering with tag lines; **nothing is dropped**; tool tethers on every operative at height.
- **Plant/pedestrian interface (admin):** banksman/traffic marshal controls all vehicle and plant movement across the footpath; deliveries off-peak; signage and lighting.
- **Continuity:** the exclusion zone is established at Step 1 and stood down only at Step 8, in stages, with a final housekeeping and surface inspection **before the public are readmitted**.
- **CDM Reg 13(4) duty:** as Principal Contractor, secure the site so **unauthorised persons cannot access** the work area — this includes out-of-hours make-safe of the footpath interface.

## 8. Emergency & rescue arrangements (activity-specific)

Generic "call 999" is **not sufficient** for work at height — rescue plans below are rehearsed at briefing.

- **MEWP rescue (RA-10, RA-14 — primary rescue scenario):** if the operator is incapacitated or the basket cannot be lowered from the platform, the standby **ground rescue person** operates the **ground/auxiliary emergency lowering controls** to bring the basket down. All operatives are briefed on the location and operation of these controls **before Step 5**. **Suspension-trauma awareness:** a harnessed operator suspended and immobile must be recovered **rapidly**; do not leave them motionless — plan to recover within minutes and follow post-rescue casualty positioning guidance.
- **Tower rescue (RA-04, RA-10):** a casualty at height on the tower is attended by the First Aider; controlled descent via the internal ladder access where the casualty is mobile; where not, the MEWP or emergency services effect recovery. Never overload the platform during a rescue.
- **Falling-object / public injury (RA-07):** stop work; first-aid response; secure the scene; the exclusion zone contains the incident; escalate to emergency services; RIDDOR-report as applicable.
- **General provision:** trained **First Aider** and stocked first-aid kit on site every shift; **RV point** and site address briefed and posted; **nearest A&E** route confirmed; **spill kit** for minor spills; fire points and extinguishers at the compound. Emergency contacts (Site Manager, First Aider, emergency services, building duty manager for the occupied building) posted at the access point and briefed.

| A7 | Brief & rehearse **MEWP ground-rescue plan** and confirm standby rescue person before Step 5 | Admin | RA-14 | IPAF Operator / Site Supervisor | Before Step 5 (works window) |
| A8 | Establish **daily weather / wind check** with recorded do-not-work thresholds from plant data plates | Admin | RA-17 | Site Supervisor | Daily, from 10 July 2026 |
| A9 | Coordinate **SIMOPS** with other trades & occupier — agree shared exclusion zones and no over-under working | Elim/Admin | RA-16 | Site Manager | Daily, from 10 July 2026 |
| A10 | Confirm **licensed waste disposal** route with transfer/consignment notes (hazardous stream separate) | Admin | RA-19 | Site Manager | Before Step 8 (works window) |

*All actions carry an owning role, a due date, a HoC tier and a hazard link; none is anonymous or "ASAP".*
